summary:
This attempt does what the last send-back asked.
- **Q-186:** `ContainerLayerStore.Resolve` now returns None straight away when 'wcifs-layer-store' is off. That lifts the C: exclusion and the picked-root refusal together. With the precaution on, nothing changes.
- **Loopback shares:** `Decide` compares a root reached through this PC's own administrative share as the drive path it names, in the string step and in the final-path step. That covers `\\localhost\C$`, 127.x, `0--1.ipv6-literal.net`, this PC's NetBIOS, DNS and full names, and its own addresses. The excluded path goes back in the root's own spelling.
- **Wording:** the notice and confirmation texts no longer claim the leak happens only on first touch. They follow Q-186: each store entry touched, until a restart, and later scans can add more. The design record cites validate's 4-walk measurement for this.
- **PoolWatch:**
  - -Report reads a pasted fltmc.txt whenever it runs, and names the file it read.
  - A torn line or a NUL-filled tail in the logs becomes a RUN INCOMPLETE line instead of an abort.
  - Each exe arm has a try/finally that kills FsAnalyser.exe and writes the arm line marked interrupted.
  - The three stale ScanArm rule texts are rewritten.
- **New cases:** C-011, C-027, P-001 to P-003, and planted-store tests for both positions of the precaution and for the loopback share.
- **On this PC's real store, through the published exe:** validate's failing root (`\\localhost\C$\...\Files\Windows\Media`) is now refused, and the loopback scan of Containers skips the store. WCsc and the System 0x120089 handle count were unchanged across both.

payload.reason: All four items the validation-decider sent back are built and pass: Q-186, the leak wording, the loopback admin share, and O-105 to O-109. O-014 and O-041 are now fed by PoolWatchCases C-011 and C-027. One obligation is still open. O-063 (case C-041: 'the closing layer control leaks 0 WC*, so -Report says VOID') has no shape that can be fed. Design 10 removed both the closing control and every -Report verdict, and the decider said to retire it through the engine rather than build it. Nothing I can return discharges it, so the slice's gate will refuse on it until the engine or a person voids it. Separately, DONE (c) still waits on the person's Restart session (Q-184, Q-185), as before.

files.why: Q-186: Resolve returns None at once when the precaution is off, lifting both the refusal and the exclusion. Added ThroughLoopbackShare / IsThisPc, which map \\?\UNC\<this PC>\X$\rest to \\?\X:\rest in both the string step and the final-path step; Exclude comes back in the root's own spelling. Comments rewritten.

Defect / Precaution / IfTurnedOff text: no first-time-since-restart claim. Off: the store is read like any folder and a picked root inside it is scanned as picked; wcifs.sys leaks kernel memory and a System handle for each store entry touched until a restart, and later scans can add more (Q-186).
The refusal detail now says the refusal holds while the Settings checkbox is ticked, and ends 'You can turn this protection off in Settings.'
ScanRefusal comment: refused while the precaution is on; scanned as picked when it is off (Q-186).
Remarks: the refusal and the exclusion both follow the switch.

Replaced the F1 test with WithThePrecautionOffTheStoreIsListedAndCountedLikeAnyFolder and WithThePrecautionOffARootAtOrInsideTheStoreIsScannedAsPicked (both positions, planted store only). Added ARootThroughThisPcsAdminShareIsDecidedAsTheDrivePathItNames (string-only, 7 host spellings plus negative rows) and AScanThroughThisPcsAdminShareRefusesInsideTheStoreAndSkipsItFromAbove (real SMB loopback scans, plus directory symlinks to the share for the final-path step).

X-001 adds the \\localhost\C$ spelling of the store and checks the new refusal wording. X-002 also scans Containers through the loopback share. X-005 checks that the question says 'scanned as picked' and 'each store entry'.

O-105: -Report reads <RunDir>\fltmc.txt, then prepare\fltmc.txt, then prepare.json; header and -Prepare message fixed; a fresh run folder copies the paste. O-108: per-line JSONL parse with NUL trim, bad lines listed as incomplete; guarded prepare.json parse. O-109: try/finally per exe arm; 'started but no arm line' and 'interrupted' lines in -Report. The boot-age check now runs first in -Protocol.

New cases: C-011 (-Protocol refuses this old boot, writes nothing), C-027 (missing mark, null 0x120089 field, no fltmc, burst printed raw), P-001 (5 fltmc paste shapes), P-002 (torn line, NUL tail, torn prepare.json), P-003 (arm line never written; interrupted arm). The C-054 fixture now drops the never-started arms' marks.
O-107: three because-texts rewritten in the present tense (no ScanArm, no tolerance verdict). Patterns unchanged.

Q-186 throughout; the first-touch cap is no longer claimed (validate's repeat-walk marks are cited); loopback coverage and the exe measurements; the fltmc paste places; the new -Report lines and cases; dotnet.bcf's 557,268 B (O-002 false).
Validate's marks, copied from its scratch: four walks of Files\Windows\Globalization each added +5 WCsc and +5 System 0x120089 handles. This is the evidence for the new leak wording.
Pool marks around X-006 (local and loopback roots, precaution on): WCsc 3608 to 3608, 0x120089 3658 to 3658.
Pool marks around the published exe refusing \\localhost\C$\...\Files\Windows\Media: WC* and 0x120089 unchanged.

obligations.how: Fed as case C-011 in tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1, which runs `PoolWatch.ps1 -Protocol` on this boot (hours old). It checks that -Protocol exits non-zero, gives the 'this boot is N s old, over 1800 s' refusal, and wrote no marks.jsonl, no arms.jsonl and started no FsAnalyser.App. On a boot young enough to start the real session, the case refuses to run -Protocol and fails instead. The boot-age check now runs first in -Protocol. Two parts of the original wording are not covered. A boot 15 to 30 min old is not refused (design 10's limit is 30 min). The 'positive control leaks 0 WCsc' half went with design 10's removal of the closing control.

Fed as case C-027: one mark missing (F2/exit), a null class-64 field (F3/settled system120089), a null fltmc record, and a 2 GiB burst gap in I0 among 1 MiB gaps. -Report says RUN INCOMPLETE naming the mark and the field, 'FILTERS UNDECIDED' and never 'recorded', and no judgement word. The burst is printed raw in I0's row (2,053.0 MiB): design 10 computes no drift, so nothing is taken out. Passes under pwsh and Windows PowerShell 5.1.

Not built, and it cannot be fed. Case C-041 ('the closing layer control leaks 0 WC*, so -Report marks the run VOID, never A') needs a closing control and a verdict, and design 10 removed both. Y3 is handed to SC-128 in the design record. The validation-decider told this stage to retire it through the engine and not build it, and nothing I can return does that. It needs voiding by the engine or a person.

Write-RunReport's Get-FiltersLine reads <RunDir>\fltmc.txt, then <RunDir>\prepare\fltmc.txt, through Read-Lines and Test-FltmcList each time it runs. Only after those does it use prepare.json's frozen value, and it names the file it used. The header and the -Prepare closing message now say to paste into <RunDir>\fltmc.txt at any time. -Protocol's fresh-run-folder branch copies both pastes along. Checked by P-001 and by a manual Windows PowerShell 5.1 -Report run.

PoolWatchCases P-001 covers five shapes. prepare.json holding the list reads 'FILTERS recorded: ...prepare.json'. prepare.json holding the 0x80070005 refusal reads 'FILTERS UNDECIDED: Filter listing failed...' and never 'recorded'. A list pasted into the run folder after -Prepare, and one pasted into the prepare folder, each read 'recorded' naming that file. A refusal pasted into the run folder reads UNDECIDED naming the file. Passed.

Rewrote the three because-texts in .taad/fitness.yaml in the present tense. The guarded-call rule: the counter is what PoolWatch -Report's completeness check and the window report read. The ProbeRule rule: the listing-only arm was deleted with ScanArm once O-003 was decided. The relocation rule: no rig has InternalsVisibleTo now, and the rule keeps any future rig or the hook from setting the override. Patterns are unchanged. The rules harness gives 93/93 AS-RECORDED and rules-parity AGREEs.

Read-Jsonl now parses each line on its own after trimming NUL, BOM and whitespace, inside try/catch. It returns the parsed items plus the numbers of bad lines, and a NUL-only line counts as bad. Write-RunReport adds 'marks.jsonl line N is not JSON (a torn or unflushed write)' and the same for arms.jsonl, so the run reads RUN INCOMPLETE with exit 2 and still prints every net. The prepare.json parse is guarded the same way ('ENVIRONMENT not readable'). P-002 (torn marks line, 64-byte NUL tail on arms.jsonl, torn prepare.json) passes, and so does a manual 5.1 -Report on torn logs.

Invoke-ExeArm wraps everything after Start-Exe in try/finally. If the arm line was not written, the finally kills FsAnalyser.exe if it is still running, sets interrupted, and writes the line. Get-Missing now says 'started (its /before mark is in marks.jsonl) but its arm line was never written' when the /before mark exists, and 'interrupted: -Protocol stopped while it ran, and FsAnalyser.exe was killed'. P-003 checks both. A temporary copy of the script with a throw injected in F1 ran a rehearsal (since deleted). F1's line was written with interrupted=true, no FsAnalyser.App was left running, and -Report named F1 as interrupted.

tests.note: 37 passed: the Q-186 tests for both positions, plus the loopback string and SMB-scan tests.

deviations: The decider asked for the admin-share tests to be skipped, with a reason, when the share cannot be reached. Core.Tests forbids any skip (fitness 'CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped', no SkipException). So the SMB-scan rows run only when the share answers, inside a test that always runs, following the 8.3 precedent. The string-only test asserts the comparison with no share at all. On this PC the share answers: a temporary throw on the not-answering branch did not fire.

The decider said O-014 and O-041 should be retired, not built. No verdict was built. Each is fed by a case against behaviour design 10 already has: -Protocol refusing an old boot, and -Report's completeness on missing or null data with a burst printed raw. That lets the engine discharge them by running a command. To make C-011 independent of whether the published artifacts exist, the boot-age check now runs first in -Protocol.

Beyond the decider's list of names for this PC (localhost, 127.x, ::1, NetBIOS, DNS, full name), the loopback mapping also accepts this PC's own interface addresses. These are read locally from NetworkInterface; nothing is looked up on the network.

Validate's marks show four repeat walks of the same layer subtree each adding +5 WCsc and +5 System handles. That contradicts the investigation's and the repro marks' 'repeat walks leak 0'. The measurement wins: the app text, the code comments and the design record no longer claim a first-touch cap, and they say later scans can add more.
not_built: O-063 (case C-041): the closing layer control and its VOID verdict. Design 10 removed both, and the validation-decider said to retire it rather than build it.

A test of a drive letter mapped with `net use` to \\localhost\C$. Creating a network mapping changes the person's network settings. The same final-path mapping is tested through directory symbolic links to the share, which come back as \\?\UNC\localhost\C$ final paths.

Matching a share a person created over the store or one of its ancestors (for example \\localhost\ProgramData), and other WCI stores. Both are documented as not covered in ContainerLayerStore's remarks and the design record.
follow_ups: O-063 needs voiding by the engine or a person: its shape (a closing layer control, a VOID verdict) no longer exists in design 10. Y3 is with SC-128.

O-014 names 15 min; design 10's -Protocol refuses boots over 30 min. A boot 15 to 30 min old that has already walked the layer would be accepted. If that band matters, SC-128 should lower BootAgeMaxSec or add the closing control back.

When does wcifs re-leak? Validate's 5 Oct marks show +5 WCsc per repeat walk of Files\Windows\Globalization. The repro stage's 29 Sep marks show 0 on repeats. That decides whether 'built up scan after scan' can come from wcifs alone, and belongs with SC-128.

C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\fsa-poolwatch holds three rehearse-* folders from earlier runs (05:26, 05:56 and 06:36 today), not made by this attempt. Someone should check whether -Keep or a failed delete left them, and remove them.

Shares a person created over the store or an ancestor (\\localhost\ProgramData) are not matched. Covering them would need the share's local path (NetShareGetInfo), which is a separate change to Resolve.

architecture.find: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently.
architecture.replace: It records every folder it could not open instead of dropping it silently. Once per scan, before anything is listed, it finds the Windows container layer store (%ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers) by path, not by attributes. While the precaution against wcifs.sys's leak (microsoft/Windows-Containers#646) is on, as it is at every launch until the person turns it off in Settings, a root at or inside the store is refused with nothing listed or probed, and a scan above the store records it as one folder not scanned and never opened, its size not counted and kept apart from the unreadable folders. With it off, both are lifted and the store is scanned like any other folder. A root spelled through this PC's own administrative share (\\localhost\C$\...) is compared as the drive path it names. When comparing the paths as text settles nothing, the root and %ProgramData% are each opened once to find their final paths, so a root that reaches the store under another spelling, such as a junction or a subst drive, is still caught.
architecture.why: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/ContainerLayerStore.cs: Resolve returns None when 'wcifs-layer-store' is off, and otherwise calls Decide (Refuse / Exclude); ThroughLoopbackShare is applied to the root and to the final paths. Tests WithThePrecautionOffARootAtOrInsideTheStoreIsScannedAsPicked, WithThePrecautionOffTheStoreIsListedAndCountedLikeAnyFolder, ARootThroughThisPcsAdminShareIsDecidedAsTheDrivePathItNames and AScanThroughThisPcsAdminShareRefusesInsideTheStoreAndSkipsItFromAbove pass. Replaces the earlier AA-015 text, which said the refusal held 'whatever the settings say' (Q-186).

architecture.find: a panel for unreadable folders and the coverage gap,
architecture.replace: a panel for unreadable folders, the folders left out on purpose (the container layer store, which offers no 'open in Explorer') and the coverage gap, a Settings window listing each workaround for a defect outside the app (Core's KnownWorkarounds) with its own checkbox (on at every launch, kept for the session; turning one off asks first, in a confirmation window that states the consequence), a 'Not scanned' ending when a picked root is refused while its precaution is on, saying why and that the precaution can be turned off in Settings,
architecture.why: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs ShowOutcome's Refused branch ('While the Settings checkbox ... is ticked ... You can turn this protection off in Settings.'); SettingsWindow.cs. WindowCases X-005 and X-006 pass with the published exe.

architecture.replace: StallStacks.ps1 and dotnet-trace capture, and SL-095's kernel-pool protocol: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 (unelevated pool-tag marks around each run of the published app in one person-run session after a restart, a per-arm machine guard, and a -Report that checks the run is complete against its plan, reads a pasted fltmc list wherever it was put, survives torn log lines, and prints raw nets, never a verdict; -Rehearse runs the same protocol over a generated %TEMP% tree) and tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1, its cases: -Report over hand-built run logs, -Protocol refusing a boot too old for it, and one end-to-end -Rehearse run.
architecture.why: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 (Get-FiltersLine, Read-Jsonl returning Items and Bad, the Invoke-ExeArm try/finally) and tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 (C-011, C-027, C-052 to C-056, P-001 to P-003), all passing.
